answer: Each agent runs inside a TEE that issues a signed “prism token” bound to the unique hardware ID and refreshed every tide cycle; the token includes a nonce that the network verifies before accepting any transaction. When a new agent appears, the ledger checks that its prism token’s hardware fingerprint does not already ripple through the registry of active IDs, rejecting duplicates instantly. To spawn a Sybil, an attacker must purchase distinct TEEs or rent cloud instances, incurring a minimum hardware‑cost of $1,200 per fake identity plus a 24‑hour lock‑up for the tide‑based re‑attestation.
